newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes lower on sickly physical market.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes lower on sickly physical market.

text.p: IPE Brent futures extended losses in the final hour of trade on Thursday against a backdrop of increasingly prominent bearish fundamentals, traders said.

July Brent settled 40 cents lower at $18.32 a barrel. June gas oil closed earlier some $3.0 lower at $165.75 a tonne putting it firmly in contango with the July contract which ended some $2.75 off at $167.75 a tonne.

Traders attributed the Brent losses partly to the sickly state of the physical North Sea Brent market which is under pressure from ample June supply, a lack of refiner demand and a shut arbitrage door to the United States
Some traders said, however, that despite these bearish factors the market had held quite well.
"Every time you think it's going to nose-dive fresh buying comes in," said one trader. "It seems to be pretty well supported around the $18.25 area."
"There's not much positive news out there at the moment on the crude front," said another trader.
Traders said the release of the International Energy Agency's (EIA) monthly report on oil market trends would give the market some focus on Friday.
